properties.name: A full export→import→export round trip preserves 3,140/3,140 nodes and changes 223 edges — all one property, REALIZES.conformance null→unchecked — and CONVERGES on the second pass, so the committed export is not in the normal form its own importer produces
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24 on the committed export at main `1ef45e5`, using the debug `reflow2-mcp` CLI end to end: `--import` the committed document into an empty store, `--export` it back out, and `--diff` the two.

RESULT:

    nodes_unchanged   3140 of 3140      design_added/removed/changed  0 / 0 / 0
    edges_unchanged  13167 of 13390     edges_added/removed             0 / 0
    edges_changed      223  — EVERY ONE of them the SAME property:
                             REALIZES.conformance   null -> "unchecked"

⭐ IT IS SEMANTICALLY LOSSLESS. Nothing is dropped and nothing changes meaning: `unchecked` is the documented default `link_artifact` gives `conformance`, so the importer is materialising a default the exporter had omitted. No node, no edge, no design content is lost in a round trip.

⭐⭐ AND IT CONVERGES — TESTED, NOT ASSUMED. Importing the ROUND-TRIPPED document and exporting again produced a file BYTE-IDENTICAL to it. So this is a ONE-TIME NORMALISATION and then a fixed point, not a drift that compounds. That distinction is the whole finding: a compounding drift would make hydrate-from-document unusable, and a one-time normalisation makes it a migration.

THE SPLIT IS HISTORICAL, AND MEASURED: of 360 `REALIZES` edges in the committed export, **137 already carry `conformance` and 223 do not**. The 223 are the ones written before the property existed; the importer fills them in. So the count is not a coincidence — it is exactly the legacy set.

🛑 WHY THIS MATTERS TODAY, INDEPENDENT OF ANY STORAGE-MODEL CHANGE. **The committed export is not in the normal form its own importer produces.** `dec:export-hash-chain` makes the export's content hash carry lineage and tamper evidence, and `compare_designs`, the git merge driver and the drift gate all read that document. So anyone who imports a colleague's export and re-exports — a restore, a machine move, a merge-driver path, a hosted hydrate — produces a **223-edge phantom diff that means nothing**, and a content hash that says the design changed when it did not. That is the same CLASS as the phantom drifts caused by the graph not branching with git, from a different cause.

⚠️ THE FIX HAS TWO DIRECTIONS AND THEY MUST AGREE, which is why this is recorded rather than patched: either the EXPORTER stops omitting the default, or the IMPORTER stops materialising it. `dec:idea-a-hosted-tier-of-many-single-writer-tenants` already names the second direction as BL-198 ("stop serializing defaults"), and flags it as a SCALING decision rather than tidiness because blob size is hydrate time. Whichever way it goes, the two sides currently disagree and the round trip is where it shows.

📌 BOUNDS, so this is not read wider than it was measured: one document, one direction, debug binary, RocksDB backend with fulltext on. It says nothing about hydrate SPEED (measured separately) and nothing about whether accumulated store state outside the design — confirmation dates, drift baselines, `write_gen`, the `.id.json`/`.sync.json` sidecars — survives the trip. Those were NOT tested here, and they remain the open risk in any move to document-as-truth.
